# Managing GitHub Automated Workflows

## Directory Structure

GitHub enforces is that all workflow .yml files must live in the root .github/workflows/ folder—everything else (scripts, helper functions, docs) can be organized cleanly into topic subfolders.

for example:

public-portal-releases/
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       ├── update-air-quality.yml          
│       ├── update-communicable-disease.yml 
│       └── update-behavioral-health.yml    
├── air-quality/
│   ├── R/
│   │   └── get_deq_pm25.R
│   └── scripts/
│       └── update_aq_data.R
├── communicable-disease/
│   ├── R/
│   └── scripts/
│       └── update_cd_data.R
├── behavioral-health/
│   ├── R/
│   └── scripts/
│       └── update_bh_data.R
└── shared/


give each topic its own rolling release tag—for example:

air-quality-latest

communicable-disease-latest

behavioral-health-latest

If two workflows run at the same time, they upload to separate releases and never overwrite or lock each other out.



## Referencing Database URLs

Stable URLs for Shiny: Always reference the specific tag name in your Shiny URLs rather than GitHub's /releases/latest/ shortcut (because /releases/latest/ redirects to whichever single release across the whole repo was created most recently)

AQ_DAILY_URL <- "https://github.com/<your-username>/public-portal-releases/releases/download/air-quality-latest/aq_daily.rds"
CD_DATA_URL  <- "https://github.com/<your-username>/public-portal-releases/releases/download/communicable-disease-latest/cd_summary.rds"


## Keeping Each Workflow Isolated in GitHub


Each .yml file in .github/workflows/ needs: 

1. Unique `concurrency` group so a weekly disease job never waits on or cancels an hourly air quality job.

2. `working-directory` pointed at that topic's subfolder so your existing source("R/...") and data/ paths keep working unchanged.

3. Topic-specific release tag in the `gh release` commands and only the R packages that specific pipeline needs.
